Is a Market Melt-Up Coming? Why Tech & Semis Are Dominating Again | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 58

Chris Verrone and Todd Sohn interpret the rebound as a return to AI, power and bank leadership, with faster risk-taking than in 2025. They discuss gold's changing behavior, software capitulation, credit versus geopolitical risk and passive semiconductor concentration. Verrone expects a possible melt-up; Eisman reports that view and emphasizes benign bank credit. Their technical indicators are hypotheses requiring defined, independent price tests. Energy's prewar uptrend explicitly challenges an exclusively war-driven account.

How he reasons here

  • Use price behavior to challenge intuitive macro narratives.
  • Oversold is a condition, not an automatic purchase signal.
  • Inspect look-through sector concentration in passive funds.
  • Separate financial contagion from geopolitical headlines.
  • Retain false signals and changing market structure when using historical analogies.

Tools and charts discussed

Mentioned in the transcript; visual charts have not all been inspected.

  • ETF net inflows versus trading volume.
  • Gold correlations and precious-metal ETF turnover.
  • Semiconductor and software index weights.
  • Software trend lines and relative performance.
  • Bank charts and credit spreads.
  • Sector relative strength and ETF launches.
